_meta.indication: CAMZYOS is a cardiac myosin inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adults with symptomatic NYHA class II-III obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) to improve functional capacity and symptoms.

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, multicenter, international, parallel-group trial; patients randomized 1:1 to a starting dose of 5 mg CAMZYOS or placebo once daily for 30 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with symptomatic NYHA class II-III obstructive HCM, LVEF ≥55%, and Valsalva LVOT peak gradient ≥50 mmHg at rest or with provocation.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary composite functional endpoint at 30 weeks: proportion of patients achieving either improvement of pVO2 by ≥1.5 mL/kg/min plus improvement in NYHA class by at least 1, or improvement of pVO2 by ≥3.0 mL/kg/min plus no worsening in NYHA class.
pivotal_trials.result: A greater proportion met the primary endpoint at Week 30 with CAMZYOS vs placebo (37% [45/123] vs 17% [22/128]; difference 19% [95% CI 9, 30]; p=0.0005).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>5% and more common than placebo) were dizziness (27% vs 18%) and syncope (6% vs 2%); syncope (0.8%) was the only adverse reaction leading to discontinuation. The principal serious risk is heart failure due to systolic dysfunction from LVEF reduction.
target_moa: Mavacamten is an allosteric and reversible inhibitor selective for cardiac myosin; it modulates the number of myosin heads entering force-generating states, reducing cross-bridge formation and shifting myosin toward an energy-sparing super-relaxed state, thereby reducing dynamic LVOT obstruction.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF HEART FAILURE — CAMZYOS reduces LVEF and can cause heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Echocardiogram assessments of LVEF are required before and during treatment; initiation is not recommended in patients with LVEF <55%. Concomitant use of certain CYP450 inhibitors/inducers is contraindicated, and CAMZYOS is available only through a REMS.

rems.type: CAMZYOS is available only through a restricted program, the CAMZYOS REMS Program, because of the risk of heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. Prescribers and pharmacies must be certified and patients must enroll and comply with ongoing monitoring.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it did not raise significant or controversial safety or efficacy issues.

summary.text: CAMZYOS (mavacamten) was submitted as a standard-review NDA received January 28, 2021 and approved April 28, 2022 for symptomatic NYHA class II-III obstructive HCM based on the single pivotal Phase 3 EXPLORER-HCM trial; approval carries a boxed warning and a REMS for heart failure risk, with no accelerated-approval, breakthrough, orphan, or fast-track designations stated.

In the Phase 3 trial EXPLORER-HCM, mavacamten was administered to adults with obstructive HCM (oHCM) whose baseline ejection fraction was at least 55%, with a peak LVOT gradient of at least 50 mmHg as assessed by echocardiography at rest, after Valsalva maneuver, or post-exercise (confirmed by echocardiography core laboratory interpretation), an LVOT gradient of at least 30 mmHg with Valsalva maneuver, and NYHA class II or III symptoms at screening. Monotherapy with beta-blockers, verapamil, or diltiazem was allowed. Concomitant therapy with beta-blocker with diltiazem or beta-blocker with verapamil was excluded, as was monotherapy with disopyramide or ranolazine. Prior treatment with cardiotoxic agents such as doxorubicin

Based on the pivotal EXPLORER-HCM trial, it can be fairly concluded that the Applicant satisfied the statutory requirement for substantial evidence of effectiveness to support approval of mavacamten for the proposed indication.

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Camzyos (mavacamten) capsules to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of heart failure due to systolic dysfunction.

requirement.text: PMR 4257-1: Conduct a worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Camzyos during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant; assess infant outcomes through at least the first year of life.

Assess infant outcomes through at least the first year of life. Specify the minimum number of patients in the protocol.
